macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rebound as technology shares recover
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite rose about 1.1% and the S&P 500 gained roughly 1%, while the Dow was little changed after the previous session’s sharp sell-off. Semiconductor stocks led the rebound, with Nvidia, Micron, AMD and Tesla among the notable gainers.[1][2]

items.title: October U.S. jobs report strengthens rate-hike expectations
items.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, exceeding expectations, while unemployment fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. Markets increased the probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December to about 77%, and two-year Treasury yields rose.[1][10]

items.title: Airbnb shares surge after strong quarterly earnings
items.summary: Airbnb shares jumped 11.7% after the company reported third-quarter earnings of $3.16 per share, up 43% year over year and above analyst expectations. Revenue rose 19% to $4.87 billion.[1][4]

items.title: Bank of England raises rates amid inflation concerns
items.summary: The Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time in more than three years. Governor Andrew Bailey indicated that additional tightening could be needed, depending partly on developments in the Iran war and their effect on inflation.[2]

items.title: Global markets assess AI spending and regulatory risks
items.summary: Investors continued to reassess the cost and regulatory risks surrounding artificial-intelligence infrastructure after a severe technology sell-off. Global equity funds nevertheless recorded a seventh consecutive week of inflows through November 4.[3]

items.title: Atlassian shares fall after quarterly results
items.summary: Atlassian shares declined 14.1% following the release of its first-quarter results, weighing on the software sector as technology stocks remained volatile.[5]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market plunges amid regulatory and macroeconomic concerns
items.summary: The global cryptocurrency market fell sharply over the past 24 hours, with total capitalization reported near $2.54 trillion. Bitcoin declined about 3.2% to $75,717, while Ethereum fell 4.5% to $2,238; XRP dropped 7.3% and Solana 2.2%. Liquidations reached roughly $1.22 billion as investors reacted to U.S. regulatory uncertainty, a stronger dollar and broader risk-off markets.

items.title: Nigeria tightens crypto rules and bans algorithmic stablecoins
items.summary: Nigeria introduced new licensing and reserve requirements for crypto payment-service providers and banned algorithmic stablecoins as authorities expand central-bank oversight of the sector.

items.title: Core Scientific plans to exit Bitcoin mining for AI hosting
items.summary: Core Scientific reportedly plans to leave Bitcoin mining by the end of 2026 and redirect its infrastructure toward artificial-intelligence hosting. The move reflects continued pressure on mining economics and growing demand for data-center capacity.

items.title: Greece approves 10% crypto capital-gains tax
items.summary: Greece approved a 10% tax on cryptocurrency capital gains, including a €500 exemption, adding a new fiscal framework for digital-asset investors.

items.title: iOS exploit reportedly drains $5.57 million from crypto users
items.summary: The DarkSword exploit kit reportedly stole approximately $5.57 million from cryptocurrency users through an iOS-related attack, highlighting continuing risks from mobile-wallet compromises.

items.title: House Democrats consider crypto market-structure bill with stronger SEC role
items.summary: House Democrats are reportedly discussing a future crypto market-structure bill that could expand the SEC’s authority, reduce the CFTC’s role and include ethics restrictions for federal officials. The discussions follow stalled progress on the CLARITY Act.

items.title: SEC staff reportedly declines enforcement recommendation over Canton Coin
items.summary: The SEC’s Division of Corporation Finance reportedly said it would not recommend enforcement over Canton Coin’s programmatic minting, characterizing the token as a digital commodity rather than a security.

items.title: Hong Kong passes crypto-asset reporting framework legislation
items.summary: Hong Kong’s Legislative Council reportedly passed legislation implementing the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, expanding tax-information reporting obligations for crypto-asset service providers.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GOG announces Linux launcher and classic-game updates
items.summary: GOG’s first showcase revealed that GOG Galaxy is in development for Linux, announced upgraded Anniversary Editions for six Wing Commander games, and introduced a new publishing label and social features.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day teases Season 2 legacy content
items.summary: The Coalition is preparing a second season featuring legacy maps, modes and skins, following the return of the Guardian mode and the addition of a new Horde mission.

items.title: Unity reportedly in $21.5 billion buyout talks
items.summary: Unity Software is reportedly discussing a potential buyout involving Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund. No agreement has been reached, and negotiations remain ongoing.

items.title: M80 acquires Boston Breach Call of Duty League franchise
items.summary: Esports organization M80 has acquired the Boston Breach franchise and plans to compete as M80 Boston, in what it describes as its largest organizational investment.

items.title: Major November releases drive gaming-related time off
items.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever and a remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time reportedly launched this week, ahead of Grand Theft Auto 6’s scheduled November 19 release.

items.title: Major publishers adopt accessibility feature tags
items.summary: Electronic Arts, Nintendo of America, Riot Games, Ubisoft and YouTube Playables have joined Xbox in using Accessible Games Initiative tags that identify features such as narrated menus, subtitles and button remapping.
